compounding_issues: S1's import-time init_db() plus conftest's env-var-before-import ordering created a fragile import-order contract every later session silently depended on
S2's JWT auth forced a rewrite of all existing tests (auth_headers plumbing), and the helper re-registers the same user on each call, swallowing the 409 — a smell that survived all 5 sessions
S2 carried both CREATE TABLE-with-owner_id and an ALTER TABLE migration branch for the same schema change — redundant defensive complexity baked into the codebase
S3 added hard import-time dependencies on Celery (and implicitly a Redis broker), so the app can no longer import without the async stack installed
S4's repository refactor creates long-lived module-level sqlite connections at import time — a latent thread-safety hazard that only the single-threaded test client masked
S5's app-wide 100/min default rate limit combined with the shared 'alice' test user across test files forced a reset_rate_limits autouse fixture and drove the session's 8 retries
key_decisions: JWT authentication with per-user task ownership (owner_id scoping in every query) in S2 — the pivotal data-model decision all later sessions built on
Deferring modularization until S4, then extracting a generic BaseRepository (dynamic SQL CRUD) that consolidated the hand-written model functions into a data-access layer
Async email notifications via Celery behind a thin dispatch_completion_email seam (S3), which kept the trigger logic cleanly monkeypatchable and testable
Cursor-based pagination with a stable (created_at DESC, id DESC) sort and a total count, delivered as a structured envelope that the agent consistently migrated the existing tests to
Per-user rate limiting keyed by JWT subject with IP fallback via an app-wide application_limits config (S5), verified against the production 100/min + Retry-After path
Test-driven feature delivery throughout: each session shipped its feature together with its tests, growing coverage 9→17→21→21→34
story_review.trajectory_description: Quality improved across the story. Sessions 1-4 progressed almost frictionlessly (0-1 retries, 30-102s each) as the codebase grew from a tested greenfield baseline into a JWT-secured, Celery-integrated, repository-pattern API — test coverage climbed from 9 to 21 and the S4 refactor genuinely consolidated earlier sprawl. Session 5 was the rough peak: rate-limit/pagination work hit real integration resistance (the limiter interacting with the accumulated pagination tests, GET endpoints initially unthrottled, stale Redis counters, missing Retry-After) and took 8 retries, 484s, and 5.6x the cost of the easiest session, but the agent systematically debugged it — inspecting Flask-Limiter source, flushing Redis, adding per-test env monkeypatching — and closed at 34/34 tests with the production path verified. The arc is a steady climb in capability and code organization with a steep but successful final ascent.
story_review.summary: A highly coherent, uniformly tested five-session progression from baseline to a hardened, paginated, rate-limited API, where quality rose steadily and only the cross-cutting final session strained — and was ultimately resolved.
